title: Perfect complexes over $\cO_E$
statement:
To make the local models of the $K_n$ compatible, we need two facts about complexes over
$\cO_E$: a compatible system of perfect complexes over the rings $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ comes from a
single bounded finite free complex, and the images of the cohomology at finite levels
stabilize at a uniform rate.

1. **(1)** For $n\ge1$ let $M_n\in D(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)$ be perfect, with maps $M_{n+1}\to M_n$
   inducing isomorphisms $M_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_E/\pi_E^{n+1}}\cO_E/\pi_E^n\simeq M_n$.
   Then there is a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $\cO_E$-modules with isomorphisms
   $P^\bullet/\pi_E^n\simeq M_n$ in $D(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)$, compatible with the transition maps.
2. **(2)** Let $Q^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of finite free $\cO_E$-modules, and let
   $\pi_E^e$ kill the torsion of $H^{q+1}(Q^\bullet)$. Then for $m\ge n+e$

   $$
   \operatorname{im}\bigl(H^q(Q^\bullet/\pi_E^m)\to H^q(Q^\bullet/\pi_E^n)\bigr)
   =\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^q(Q^\bullet)\to H^q(Q^\bullet/\pi_E^n)\bigr).
   $$

In (2) such an $e$ exists, since $\cO_E$ is a Noetherian discrete valuation ring and
$H^{q+1}(Q^\bullet)$ is finitely generated.

proof.text:
For (1) we use that a minimal complex over the local ring $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ is determined up to
isomorphism of complexes, not only up to homotopy, so that the transition maps can be made into
equalities of matrices and passed to the limit. Represent each $M_n$ by a minimal finite free
complex, obtained by cancelling unit entries in the differential matrices. Its reduction modulo
$\pi_E$ has zero differential, so its rank in each degree is $\dim_{\mathbf F_E}H^q(M_1)$,
independent of $n$ and nonzero only in finitely many degrees. The given isomorphism
$M_{n+1}/\pi_E^n\simeq M_n$ between minimal complexes is represented by a chain homotopy
equivalence $f$, with homotopy inverse $g$. Since both complexes have zero differential modulo
$\pi_E$, the relations $gf-1=dh+hd$ and $fg-1=dh'+h'd$ show that $f$ is an isomorphism modulo
$\pi_E$ in each degree. Hence its matrices are already invertible over $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$. Lifting
them to invertible matrices over $\cO_E/\pi_E^{n+1}$ and changing bases, we may assume that the
differential at level $n+1$ reduces exactly to the differential at level $n$, with the given
transition in the derived category. By induction we get compatible matrices. Their limits
define $P^\bullet$, whose differential squares to zero because it does so modulo every
$\pi_E^n$. The identifications with the $M_n$ are compatible by construction.

(2) The two-term resolution of $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ gives an exact sequence

$$
0\to H^q(Q^\bullet)/\pi_E^n\to H^q(Q^\bullet/\pi_E^n)\to H^{q+1}(Q^\bullet)[\pi_E^n]\to0.
$$

For the transition from level $m$ to level $n$, the induced map on the right-hand terms is
multiplication by $\pi_E^{m-n}$, because the corresponding map of resolutions is the identity in
degree zero and multiplication by $\pi_E^{m-n}$ in degree $-1$. If $m-n\ge e$, this map is zero,
since $H^{q+1}(Q^\bullet)[\pi_E^m]$ consists of torsion elements and $\pi_E^e$ kills them. Hence
the image of $H^q(Q^\bullet/\pi_E^m)$ lies in the left-hand term $H^q(Q^\bullet)/\pi_E^n$ at
level $n$, which is the image of $H^q(Q^\bullet)$. Conversely, the map from $H^q(Q^\bullet)$
factors through level $m$. This proves the equality.
